toc.title: Create fact tables and dimension tables

html:
1Create fact tables and dimension tables

A star schema puts a fact table in the middle and dimension tables around it. Power BI models run best on this shape.

Table Holds Used to
Dimension Descriptions of an entity: product, customer, date, store Filter and group
Fact Events such as sales lines: dimension keys and numeric columns Summarize

The rules to remember:

  • Relationships run one-to-many from the dimension (one side) to the fact (many side).
  • A fact table has one consistent grain, for example one row per order line.
  • Do not mix dimension columns and fact columns in one table.
  • A snowflake of linked dimensions can work, but one denormalized dimension is preferred, because a hierarchy cannot span tables.
  • A junk dimension holds small flags with few values, a degenerate dimension keeps an order number in the fact table, and a factless fact table records events with no numbers.

To build the tables from a flat table, load the flat query once, then make one query per table from it. For a dimension, keep the descriptive columns and the key, then use Remove Duplicates on the key so each row appears once. For the fact table, keep the keys and the numeric columns and remove the descriptions.

Exam tip

. Dimension tables filter and group, fact tables hold keys and numbers, and the relationship runs one-to-many from the dimension to the fact. Keep one grain per fact table.

2Reference or Duplicate queries

Both commands are on the right-click menu of a query. They look alike, but they behave differently.

Reference Duplicate
What it creates A new query whose first step reads the output of the original A copy of all the steps of the original
Link to the original Follows it: a change in the original flows through Independent: later changes do not reach the copy
Maintenance The shared cleaning steps live in one place Each copy must be changed separately
Use it for Fact and dimension tables built from one flat query A variation you want to change freely

The impact of a Reference: if the original query breaks, for example when a column it uses disappears, every query that references it breaks too. The Query Dependencies view on the View tab shows which query depends on which.

A common pattern is a staging query that loads and cleans the flat table, with Reference queries for each dimension and the fact table. Then you disable load on the staging query (section 5).

Exam tip

. Reference follows the original query, and Duplicate is an independent copy of the steps. When cleaning steps change often and every derived table must pick up the change, choose Reference.

3Merge and append queries

Merge adds columns by matching rows. Append adds rows by stacking tables. Both are on the Home tab, in the Combine group.

For a merge, select the matching column in each query, and hold Ctrl to select several columns for a combined match. Pick a join kind, then use the expand button on the new column to choose the columns to bring in.

Join kind Rows in the result
Left Outer All rows from the first table and matching rows from the second
Right Outer All rows from the second table and matching rows from the first
Full Outer All rows from both tables
Inner Only matching rows
Left Anti Rows only in the first table, with no match in the second
Right Anti Rows only in the second table, with no match in the first

Matching is exact: case and spaces matter, so clean the key columns first. If the second table has duplicate keys, a left outer merge repeats rows from the first table. Merge Queries as New keeps the originals and creates a new query.

Append Queries stacks rows from two tables or three or more tables. Columns are matched by name, and a column missing in one table is filled with null. Append Queries as New creates a new query and leaves the originals unchanged. Use it for monthly tables with the same layout.

let
    Source = Sales,
    Merged = Table.NestedJoin(Source, {"ProductID"}, Product, {"ProductID"}, "Product", JoinKind.LeftOuter),
    Expanded = Table.ExpandTableColumn(Merged, "Product", {"ProductKey"})
in
    Expanded
Exam tip

. Merge adds columns and append adds rows. Left Anti returns rows in the first table that have no match in the second, which finds missing or orphan keys.

4Create appropriate keys for relationships

A relationship needs a single column on the one side whose values are unique. If the one-side column has duplicate values, the model refresh fails. The two key columns need matching data types.

Situation What to do
The key repeats in the dimension Remove Duplicates on the key to make one row per value
There is no usable key Add an Index Column to the dimension as a surrogate key, then bring it into the fact table with a merge
The match needs several columns Create a composite key: Merge Columns with a separator, in both tables, in the same format

Power BI relationships use one column on each side. That is why two columns that identify a row together must be combined into one key first.

let
    Source = Product,
    Unique = Table.Distinct(Source, {"ProductID"}),
    Keyed = Table.AddIndexColumn(Unique, "ProductKey", 1, 1, Int64.Type)
in
    Keyed
Exam tip

. The one side of a relationship needs a unique column; duplicates make refresh fail. Create a surrogate key with an index column, and a composite key by merging columns.

5Configure data loading for queries

Each query has settings on its right-click menu in the Queries pane. They decide what ends up in the model.

Setting Effect
Enable load On: the query becomes a table in the model. Off: it only runs when other queries use it
Include in report refresh Off: Refresh and scheduled refresh skip this query's data
Close and Apply Sends the results to the model and closes the editor; Apply keeps the editor open

Disable load for staging and intermediate queries, such as the flat table that other queries reference. They then stay out of the model, which keeps it smaller. A query that is not loaded still runs when a referencing query needs it. Turn off Include in report refresh only for data that should not change, such as a fixed lookup list.

Queries load in parallel, so the load order is not guaranteed. Never rely on one query loading before another. Express dependencies with Reference instead.

Exam tip

. Clear Enable load on staging queries so they do not become model tables. Hiding a table in Report view is different: a hidden table is still loaded.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A flat Orders query is cleaned in several steps that change often. The Product and Sales queries must always pick up those changes. What should the analyst create?

  • ADuplicate queries of Orders, which copy all of its steps
  • BAppend queries of Orders, which stack its rows
  • CReference queries of Orders, which follow its output
  • DMerge queries of Orders, which join it with itself
Show the answer

Answer: C. A Reference starts from the output of the original, so changes in the original flow through.

S2A flat Sales table holds ProductID, ProductName, Category, Amount and Quantity. Which columns belong in the Product dimension table?

  • AProductID, Amount and Quantity
  • BProductName, Category and Amount
  • CCategory, Amount and Quantity
  • DProductID, ProductName and Category
Show the answer

Answer: D. A dimension holds the key and the descriptive columns, while Amount and Quantity belong in the fact table.

S3An analyst must list the customers in the Customer table who have no rows in the Sales table. Which join kind should the merge use, with Customer as the first table?

  • ALeft Anti, which keeps rows only in the first table
  • BInner, which keeps only the rows that match in both
  • CLeft Outer, which keeps all rows from the first table
  • DFull Outer, which keeps all rows from both tables
Show the answer

Answer: A. Left Anti returns the first-table rows that have no match in the second.

S4Twelve monthly tables have the same columns, and the analyst needs one table with all rows. The originals must stay unchanged. Which command should be used?

  • AMerge Queries as New, matching on the date column
  • BGroup By on the month column, with All Rows
  • CPivot Column, with the month values as headers
  • DAppend Queries as New, with three or more tables
Show the answer

Answer: D. Append Queries as New stacks the rows of many tables into a new query and leaves the originals unchanged.

S5Two tables relate by Store and Date together, but Power BI relationships use one column. What should the analyst do?

  • ACreate two relationships, one for each column
  • BCreate a combined key column in both tables
  • CChange the relationship to many-to-many
  • DAdd an index column to the fact table only
Show the answer

Answer: B. Merging the two columns into one composite key in both tables gives each relationship a single column to match.

S6A flat Orders query is referenced by the Product and Sales queries. How do you keep Orders from becoming a table in the model?

  • AClear Enable load for the Orders query
  • BClear Include in report refresh for Orders
  • CHide the Orders table in Report view
  • DDelete the Orders query after applying
Show the answer

Answer: A. Clearing Enable load keeps the query out of the model while the referencing queries still use it.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is the difference between Reference and Duplicate?

Show the answer

Reference follows the original query, and Duplicate is an independent copy of its steps.

R2Which join kind returns all rows from both tables?

Show the answer

Full Outer.

R3How do you create a surrogate key?

Show the answer

Add an Index Column to the deduplicated dimension.

R4Does merge add rows or columns, and does append add rows or columns?

Show the answer

Merge adds columns, and append adds rows.

R5Is the load order of queries guaranteed?

Show the answer

No, queries load in parallel.

R6In which direction does a star schema relationship run?

Show the answer

One-to-many, from the dimension to the fact table.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Star schema dimensions filter and group; facts hold keys and numbers; one-to-many from dimension to fact; one grain
Reference follows the original; changes flow through; one place to maintain; breaks if the original breaks
Duplicate independent copy of the steps; later changes do not reach it
Merge adds columns; Left Outer, Right Outer, Full Outer, Inner, Left Anti, Right Anti; exact match
Append adds rows; two tables or three or more; matched by name; Append as New keeps originals
Keys unique one side; Remove Duplicates; Index Column as surrogate key; Merge Columns for a composite key
Loading Enable load off for staging; Include in report refresh; Close and Apply; load order not guaranteed
